Thin rye and barley flatbreads cooked in a hot dry pan, spread with butter and topped with smoked salmon, sour cream, dill and lingonberry jam. Mix 120g rye flour, 80g barley or plain flour, half a tsp baking powder, a pinch of salt, 20g melted butter and about 150ml warm milk into a soft dough. Divide into 8 and roll very thin. Cook in a hot dry pan for 1 to 2 minutes a side until speckled. Butter while warm and top with 200g smoked salmon, sour cream, a little lingonberry jam and dill.
M: Klaus's juniper beef stew with mash
the big cabin in the woods full of carved toys

Beef chuck browned and simmered for hours with onion, carrot, juniper, thyme and a spoon of blackcurrant jam until it falls apart, with buttery mash. Brown 1.2kg diced beef chuck in batches. Add 2 sliced onions and 3 carrots in chunks and cook 5 minutes. Stir in 1 tbsp flour, 6 crushed juniper berries, thyme, 1 tbsp blackcurrant jam and 750ml beef stock. Cover and simmer for 3 hours until the beef falls apart. Boil 1kg potatoes and mash with 60g butter and 100ml milk. Serve the stew over the mash.
Jesper's spoiled life before the island

Duck breasts scored and rendered skin side down until crisp, finished in the oven, sliced over a creamy potato gratin with a glossy cherry and balsamic sauce. Layer 1kg thinly sliced potatoes in a dish with 300ml cream, garlic and salt and bake at 180C for 1 hour. Score the skin of 4 duck breasts and start skin side down in a cold pan, then cook over medium heat for 8 minutes to render. Flip and roast at 200C for 6 minutes. Rest. Pour off most of the fat, add 200g pitted cherries, 2 tbsp balsamic, 1 tbsp honey and 150ml stock and reduce until glossy.
W: Gingerbread dough of butter, golden syrup, ginger and cinnamon cut into envelope shapes, baked at 180C for 10 minutes, piped with white icing and a red seal.
K: the Sámi girl who wins everyone over

Tart lingonberry cordial simmered with sugar and cinnamon, served warm in mugs with an orange slice, or poured over ice and topped with soda. Simmer 300g frozen lingonberries or cranberries with 150g sugar, a cinnamon stick and 500ml water for 10 minutes. Mash well and strain through a sieve, pressing on the fruit. Add 500ml more water and the juice of an orange. To serve warm, heat gently and pour into mugs with an orange slice. To serve cold, pour over ice and top with soda water.
